setup.kv_cache: enabled on BOTH draft and target
setup.baseline: plain target generation WITH KV cache (honest baseline)

theory_check.note: predicted ratio falls monotonically with K, matching the measured speedup fall 0.46 -> 0.36. K=1 is forward-count-neutral (1.000 at alpha=1); every K>1 is a net loss on forward count even at perfect acceptance, because 2K forwards buy at most K+1 tokens.

conclusion: NEGATIVE. Acceptance is high (72.8% at K=1) but speedup is still 0.36-0.46x. Speculative decoding needs the target forward to be much more expensive than the draft forward; at 1.5M-2.6M non-embedding parameters both forwards are latency-bound by per-op dispatch overhead, not arithmetic, so the 2K forwards per round cost roughly 2x plain decoding regardless of acceptance. The method is not wrong; the models are too small for it to pay.
caveats: prompt is only 16 tokens and generation only 32, so the KV cache is tiny and recomputation would have been cheap anyway
single prompt; speedup is a latency measurement and is noisy at these durations (0.04-0.10 s)
